manuscripts.title: Personal Identity Debate: Physiological Theory Versus Psychological Theory
manuscripts.abstract:
What does being the person that we are from one day to the next essentially consist? What change can 
a person survives and still remains the same person? These questions remain fundamental/exigent in 
the personal identity debate. What in essence and specifically constitutes a man’s/person’s identity? 
Some theories have emerged at resolving the debate, chief among them are the physiological and 
psychological theories of personal identity. The aim of the work is to examine these theories, consider 
their strengths and weaknesses and attempt to rationalize the theory that clearly and succinctly 
explicates the core elements and the definitive attribute(s) of a person’s identity. The work argued that 
though the merits of both cannot be entirely dispensed with, when considered independently, none 
necessarily resolved the problem. The work employed the method of analysis and concludes by 
proposing the reverse constructive consciousness approach to the problem.

manuscripts.abstract:
As a result of elevated sexual risk behaviors among youth in Ilorin metropolis areas, millions of youths 
face sexual and reproductive health challenges, including high rate of an unfulfilled needs for 
contraceptives, unintended pregnancy, and unsafe abortions. To develop their skills and prevent 
youth’s sexual activity from being unsafe, especially in Ilorin metropolis, teachers and peers were 
advised that teaching adolescents about reproductive health should be carried out. This study aims to 
investigate the impact of community education on pre-marital sex among youth in Ilorin metropolis. 
This research was a pre-experimental quantitative approach with a one-group. The survey used in this 
study had 240 respondents, samples were collected using a purposeful sampling process. In this 
analysis, the independent variable was peer education, while the dependent variable was the 
prevention of sexual risk activity among adolescents. The Wilcoxon sign-rank test data analysis 
showed that there were no significant differences in the prevention of sexual risk behavior among 
adolescents in Ilorin metropolis areas at pre – and post-sexual education through p-value peer 
education. There is no significant impact on reducing adolescent sexual risk behaviours in Ilorin 
metropolis through peer education. The media may significantly influence the prevention of the 
conduct of Ilorin metropolis area at sexual risk. To prevent sexual risk behavior among youth in Ilorin 
metropolis, further research is recommended to find out the best intervention using more profound 
internal and external relevant variables and media impact association study

manuscripts.title: Loan Regulations Compliance and Profitability of Saving and Credit  Cooperatives in Rwanda: A Case of Selected Umurenge Saving and Credit  Cooperatives (SACCOs) of Kigali City
manuscripts.abstract:
This study aimed at examining the effect of loan regulations compliance on profitability of saving and 
credit cooperatives in Rwanda. The problem statement indicated that non-performing loans among 
SACCOs have increased in 2020 which largely reflects the impact of COVID-19 containment 
measures on firms financed by the banking sector. Loan managements related to the restructured loans 
were identified as a key risk that is challenging Saccos and at the end of June 2020, the financial 
institutions provided payment relief to their borrowers negatively affected by COVID-19. This 
research employed a descriptive research design to provide an in-depth understanding of the numerical 
data collected. All participants were administered a questionnaire, which served as the main research 
instrument, and all participants completed it. The data was analyzed using the Statistical Package for 
Social Sciences, and the outcomes were displayed in analytical tables that emphasized the essential 
findings and conclusions of the study. The findings of hypothesis indicate that model summary of 
profitability results showed the adjusted R2 of 0.698 indicating that loan regulations compliance 
contribute to profitability by 69.8% while 30.2% of profitability comes from other variable which not 
include in model.

manuscripts.title: Effect of Financial Planning on Quality Service Delivery in  Telecommunication Companies in Rwanda
manuscripts.abstract:
This study investigated the contribution of financial planning on quality service delivery in 
telecommunication companies in Rwanda. The target population of this study is 103 respondents 
participated in this study. Structured, validated and reliable questionnaire was used. Based on 
the findings, results of the multiple regression showed that the adjusted R2
is 0.730 representing 
73.0% indicating that the financial planning components contribute to the quality service delivery. 
From ANOVA Table, the F-test is 70.093 has a p-value = 0.000. This implies that all financial 
planning components variables jointly have positive and significant effect on quality service 
delivery. Therefore, our null hypothesis which stated that there is no significant effect of financial 
planning components on quality service delivery in selected telecommunication companies in 
Rwanda is not accepted at all levels of significance. The study concluded that financial planning 
contributes positively to quality service delivery in telecommunication companies in Rwanda. It 
was recommended that during budgetary allocations, each department should be given a chance 
to participate in financial planning.

manuscripts.title: Contribution of Nurturing Learning Environment to Achieving Teaching  Objectives in Rwanda: Evidence from Selected Secondary Schools in Gasabo  District
manuscripts.abstract:
This study investigated the contribution of nurturing a learning environment to achieving teaching 
objectives in Rwanda. Through the descriptive research design, the researcher collected and 
analysed data from respondents. Regression research design was used because the researcher 
measured the relationship between the variables of the study. For this particular study, the 
population is 78 teachers of 6 selected public secondary schools in the Gasabo district. Those are 
14 teachers from GS Remera Catholic, 12 teachers from GS Kimironko I, 13 teachers from GS 
Musave, 11 teachers from GS Rugando, 13 teachers from GS Gisozi and 15 teachers from GS 
Kabuga. These schools were selected because they are Gasabo district public schools, which are 
fully funded by the government. To measure the relationship between Nurturing learning 
environment and achieving teaching objectives, regression analysis was used and the results 
indicated that the adjusted coefficient of determination was 0.948. This implies that the predictors 
of a nurturing learning environment affect the achievement of teaching objectives in secondary 
schools of the Gasabo district in Rwanda by 94.8%. In the end, schools in the Gasabo district are 
recommended to come up with strategies to increase students’ graduation rates since a large 
number of respondents disagreed that all of the enrolled students successfully finished their 
studies.

manuscripts.title: Modeling Inflation in Rwanda using Random Forest technique
manuscripts.abstract:
This study aims to model inflation in Rwanda using key economic indicators, namely the Consumer 
Price Index (CPI), international commodity prices (crude oil and fertilizers), and the Real Effective 
Exchange Rate (REER). Two regression models, Linear Regression and Random Forest Regression, 
are employed to understand the relationship between these indicators and inflation. The Random 
Forest Regression model significantly outperforms the Linear Regression model, demonstrating 
superior predictive performance with a Mean Squared Error (MSE) of 237.37 and an R-squared (R²) 
of 0.93. In comparison, the Linear Regression model achieved an MSE of 1304.93 and an R² of 0.64. 
The ability of the Random Forest model to capture complex nonlinear relationships and interactions 
among the predictors underscores its suitability for predicting inflation in Rwanda. These findings 
provide valuable insights for policymakers and economists in managing inflationary trends.

manuscripts.title: The Role of Quality Assurance in Responding to global Education Trends  among Higher Learning Institutions in Rwanda. A Case of the University of  Rwanda (UR), Adventist University of Central Africa (AUCA), University of  Kigali (UoK), and Kepler College
manuscripts.abstract:
The study at hand sought to investigate the role of quality assurance in responding to global emerging 
trends among higher learning institutions in Rwanda. The specific objectives were to establish the global 
education trends among higher learning institutions in Rwanda, to find out how quality assurance responds 
to the global education trends among higher learning institutions in Rwanda, to investigate how the 
selected higher learning institutions deal with global education trends, and to suggest ways through which 
selected higher learning institutions can adequately deal with global education trends in Rwanda. The 
study was quantitative. Researchers used data collection techniques such as documentation and 
questionnaire, to gather data. The interpretation of data was done using SPSS (Statistical Package for the 
Social Sciences) for statistical analysis and make informed decisions based on empirical evidence. During 
data analysis and interpretation of results, it was revealed that the mean for all variables is greater than the 
standard deviation, an indication that the situation in Rwanda’s higher learning institutions is not worse as 
far as global education trends are concerned. 
The findings revealed that quality assurance plays a big role in responding to global education trends 
among Rwanda’s higher learning institutions. Global education trends such as Technology integration and 
digital learning, Personal and paced learning, Blended and hybrid learning, Science, Technology, 
Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM) and the integration of the Arts (STEAM) education, Global 
competency and cross-cultural skills, Social-emotional learning, Inclusive and equitable education, 
Professional Development for Educators, Education for sustainability, Lifelong learning and upskilling,

confidence interval. From February 22 to 24, 2022 a number of 200 questionnaires were 
distributed to students during the general assembly meetings and class meetings. Only 121 
questionnaires were returned for data analysis. The study used both descriptive and correlational 
research design to design the research questions formulate research objectives and analyze data
using SPSS. V22. Findings showed that learning styles (ß=0.329; 0.05<sig. =0.029) and studentteacher interaction (ß=0.283; 0.05<sig. =0.006) affect academic performance at the Adventist 
University of Central Africa, Rwanda. It was recommended to put en emphasis on teaching 
materials and adequate facilities for the sake of variety in the learning process. It was also

manuscripts.title: Effect of Capital Structure on Return on Assets of Selected Manufacturing  Companies in Rwanda
manuscripts.abstract:
The study assessed the effect of capital structure on return on assets of manufacturing companies 
in Rwanda. Selected companies were: BRALIRWA Plc and CIMERWA Plc. This is due to the 
confirmation that, Rwandan companies have reported an average lower profitability level 
compared to regional countries particularly Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania. Capital structure was 
evaluated through Debt to Asset Ratio and Debt-to-Equity Ratio. The target population of this 
study constituted the financial reports of BRALIRWA and CIMERWA Plc for the year: 2018; 2019; 
2020; 2021 and 2023. The reason of selecting these two companies is their long experience within 
the business sector in Rwanda. The second reason was the easy accessibility of their financial 
reports. Therefore, it was reasonable that these two companies would provide an accurate 
representation of the manufacturing sector in Rwanda. The study was carried out using the expost factor research design where data were extracted from financial reports of selected 
companies from the periods of 2018 to 2022. The data collected from the financial reports were 
analyzed. The results in multiple regression analysis revealed that the Capital structure 
components contribute to the ROA in selected companies per 41.6%. The F-test is 5.583 has a pvalue = 0.000. This implies that all Capital structure components variables jointly have positive 
and significant effect on ROA in selected companies. Based on the result showed from the test of 
hypothesis, which states that there is no significant effect of capital structure (Debt to asset Ratio 
and Debt-to-Equity Ratio) on the return on assets of BRALIRWA Plc and CIMERWA Plc was 
rejected at 5% level of significance. Some weaknesses were found and researchers recommend 
selected companies to monitor the source of the money that are used where they have to encourage 
marketing in order to avoid the dominance of debts in their capital.

manuscripts.title: Contribution of Employee Motivation to Task Accomplishment in SMEs in  Rwanda: Evidence from Textile Industies (Dikam Fashion and New Kigali  Designers) in Kigali
manuscripts.abstract:
This study investigated the impact of employee motivation on task accomplishment in SMEs in 
Rwanda. A descriptive research approach was used, and questionnaires were distributed to 153 
respondents from DIKAM and New Kigali Designer. Regression analysis was adopted to 
statistically analyze the contribution of employee motivation on task accomplishment. The results 
indicated that the adjusted R2
is 0.231 representing 23.1%, indicating that the employee motivation 
components included in the model explains a relatively small portion of the variation in task 
accomplishment, while 0.769 representing 76.9% of task accomplishment is likely due to other 
factors that are not included in the model. According to the ANOVA Table, the F- test of 10.114 is
statistically significant with p < 0.05 indicated that the variables used in the model have a
goodness of fit and that are good predictors of task accomplishment. Therefore, H0 which states
that there is no significant effect of employee motivation components on task accomplishment is
rejected at all levels of significance. The study recommends prioritizing fair and competitive 
payment, fostering a positive working environments, and providing training to motivate 
employees. This can help address the operational challenges SMEs face, resulting in low 
performance and high failure rates.

manuscripts.title: Peculiarities of Kinyarwanda Proper Names: A Paradigm Shift in Three  Distinctive Historical Phases
manuscripts.abstract:
Proper names of persons and places embed extensive sociolinguistic, cultural, and historical 
aspects in the life of any nation. Thus, they have caught the researcher’s attention because of the 
cultural and historical heritage they preserve in the context of language contact. From one place to 
another, and one specific period to another, anthroponyms and toponyms offer a wide range of 
research because of the scientific curiosity researchers have as to know why the name of person or 
place exists, where it comes from, who named it, and when it was named so. In other words, the 
research is carried within spatial and temporal scope. Anthroponymy is the study of proper names 
of human beings, both individual and collective, while toponymy is the study of proper names of 
places. This paper aims at researching on person and place proper names embedding cultural and 
historical features to understand, explain, and preserve a people’s culture and history for a given 
period of time. The method used to research is descriptive and is based on the materials collected 
and observed from various sources. Therefore, this study focuses on specific topologies and periods 
which have marked the Rwandan history

manuscripts.title: Effect of Risk Management on Reduction of Non-Performing Loans of Selected  Commercial Banks in Rwanda
manuscripts.abstract:
This study investigated the effect of risk management on reduction of non-performing loans in 
commercial banks in Rwanda. This is due to the constant affirmation that profitability of commercial 
banks keep decreasing. Objective of the study is to assess the effect of risk management on nonperforming loans in commercial banks in Rwanda. Researchers assume that there is no significant 
effect of risk management on reduction of non-performing loans in commercial banks in Rwanda. 
This research used descriptive survey research design. Population of the study are 76 employees of 
Equity bank and Cogebank. These are composed of all manager, head of department, credit team, risk 
management team, audit team and financial department team of both Equity Bank Rwanda Plc 
headquarter and Cogebanque Rwanda Plc headquarter. The researcher used universal sampling 
technique and selected all the identified members of the population as the part of the study. Results 
for hypothesis testing indicated that the adjusted R2 is 0.880 indicating that the risk management 
components contribute to the reduction of non-performing loans by 88.0%, while 0.120 representing 
12.0% of reduction of non-performing loans comes from other variables that are not included in the 
model test. The selected commercial banks were recommended to find ways to improve their 
profitability levels since both of them were experiencing low levels of ROA of around 1 to 2%, yet 
the accepted good level of ROA is 5%.

manuscripts.title: Effects of Teamwork on Teachers’ Performance in Selected Schools. A Case of  Kinyinya Sector, Gasabo District

teamwork. Employee performance was found be increased by teamwork from various evidence. 
Studies were conducted in different domains, and few were conducted in the education sectors 
specifically in Rwanda. Therefore, the current study aimed to assess the effects of teamwork on 
teachers’ performance in selected schools in Gasabo District, Kinyinya Sector in Rwanda.
The study adopted a quantitative approach cross-sectional design. It involved 140 teachers selected 
from the three schools in Kinyinya Sector, Gasabo District. The sample was chosen using a 
proportionate stratified random sampling strategy then a simple random sample. To gather data a selfadministered questionnaire was employed. SPSS version 20.0 was used to analyze the data.

relationship with teachers’ performance. Team trust and team spirit positively affect the teachers’ 
performance. Team trust showed a statistical significance while team spirit did not. Team members 
‘abilities showed a non-significant negative effect on teachers’ performance. Therefore, the study 
recommended ensuring a working environment that inspires team trust among teachers.

manuscripts.title: Modeling Inflation in Rwanda using Random Forest technique
manuscripts.abstract:
This study aims to model inflation in Rwanda using key economic indicators, namely the Consumer 
Price Index (CPI), international commodity prices (crude oil and fertilizers), and the Real Effective 
Exchange Rate (REER). Two regression models, Linear Regression and Random Forest Regression, 
are employed to understand the relationship between these indicators and inflation. The Random 
Forest Regression model significantly outperforms the Linear Regression model, demonstrating 
superior predictive performance with a Mean Squared Error (MSE) of 237.37 and an R-squared (R²) 
of 0.93. In comparison, the Linear Regression model achieved an MSE of 1304.93 and an R² of 0.64. 
The ability of the Random Forest model to capture complex nonlinear relationships and interactions 
among the predictors underscores its suitability for predicting inflation in Rwanda. These findings 
provide valuable insights for policymakers and economists in managing inflationary trends.

performance in secondary education in Rwanda, G.S. SHA and G.S. Nduba. The study used

objectives of the study and write the research questions. All 191 respondents answered questions on 
the questionnaire which formed the base for analysis. The analysis and interpretations focused on the 
data collection from the targeted sample in 2022. The main purpose of this study was to examine 
impact of class size on students’ academic performance in secondary education in Rwanda, G.S. SHA 
and G.S. Nduba as a case study. Findings indicated that class size does not influence the academic 
performance of students at GS SHA and GS NDUBA (ß=.449; p-value=.114). Findings showed that there 
is a high significant influence of student participation on academic performance at GS SHA and GS 
NDUBA (ß=1.370; p-value=.000). I recommend Head teachers to improve marking students in their 
homework, test, and classroom exercises. To recommend schools management to equip the library rooms 
with all books needed in lower secondary school at G.S SHA and G.S NDUBA.

manuscripts.title: School Instruction Practices and Students’ Performance in Public Secondary  Schools in Rwanda evidence from Ruhango District, Southern Province
manuscripts.abstract:
For the past nine consecutive years, over 10% of secondary school students nationwide have failed in 
their public exams, with a 13% failure rate in Division I, consistent with the Southern Province's 
situation according to MINEDUC (2020). This study investigates the impact of instructional practices 
on student performance in public secondary schools in Ruhango district, Southern Province, Rwanda. 
The research design used correlations and regression to express relationships between variables, with 
a total population of 307 individuals, including District Directors of Education, head teachers, and 
teachers, with 74 teachers, 18 head teachers, and one DDE in the sample. Data collection instruments 
included documentary reviews and questionnaires, and both descriptive and inferential statistics were 
used for analysis. The Cronbach's Alpha Coefficient was 0.81, indicating the instrument's reliability, 
and the F-Test was used to test factors. The study found that teacher training at school had a strong 
positive correlation with students' academic performance (r = .828**, p = .000). Instructional 
supervision practices also showed a positive relationship with academic performance (r = .700**, p = 
.000). School-based mentorship was strongly connected to academic performance (r = .784**, p = 
.000), and interactive and collaborative professional trust correlated positively with academic 
performance (r = .758**, p = .000). Additionally, school peer observation was positively correlated 
with academic performance (r = .789**, p = .000). Overall, the study concluded that school 
instructional practices significantly impact students' academic performance, with all independent 
variables having p-values below 0.01. It is recommended that MINEDUC support schools and 
educators with advanced educational resources and management training.

manuscripts.title: Student Performance Prediction Based on Machine Learning Algorithms at  the Adventist University of Central Africa
manuscripts.abstract:
In recent years, there has been a growing interest in predicting student performance in educational 
institutions using machine learning. This paper presents an approach to predict student 
performance based on data mining classification techniques. The objective was to develop a 
predictive model that can accuraely forecast student performance and identify factors that 
influence academic success. The proposed approach involves the collection of various attributes 
related to students, such as identification numbers, department, faculty, GPA earned, nationality, 
place of birth, religion, gender, student absence days, parents' school satisfaction, and principal 
pass. These attributes are used as input variables for classification algorithms, including decision 
trees, logistic regression, and support vector machines. The dataset used in this study is obtained 
from University in the office of registrar and consists of historical data of students, including their 
grades and other relevant information. The dataset is preprocessed to handle missing values, 
outliers, and categorical variables. The dataset has 25 features and 2583 observations which are 
enough for training our models in doing experiment. Different classification algorithms are 
applied to the preprocessed dataset, and their performance is evaluated using various evaluation 
metrics, such as accuracy, precision. The experimental results indicate that the proposed approach 
achieves promising performance in predicting student performance. The decision tree algorithm 
outperforms other classifiers with the highest accuracy. The selected features reveal that factors 
such as previous academic performance, identification numbers, department, faculty, GPA 
earned. Influence student performance. Findings showed that the decision tree predicts student 
performance with accuracy of 99.87%. By leveraging student-related attributes and employing 
machine learning algorithms, educational institutions can enhance their decision-making 
processes and provide targeted support to students, ultimately improving overall educational 
outcomes.

manuscripts.title: Effects of Teamwork on Teachers’ Performance in Selected Schools: A Case  of Kinyinya Sector, Gasabo District
manuscripts.abstract:
People working together for a common goal and working hand in hand for its attainment are seen 
as teamwork. Various studies evidenced that teamwork increases employee performance. Studies 
were conducted in different domains, and few were conducted in the education sectors specifically 
in Rwanda. Therefore, the current study aimed to assess the effects of teamwork on teachers’ 
performance in selected schools in Gasabo District, Kinyinya Sector in Rwanda. The study 
adopted a quantitative approach cross-sectional design. It involved 140 teachers selected from the 
three schools in Kinyinya Sector, Gasabo District. The sample was chosen using a proportionate 
stratified random sampling strategy then a simple random sample. To gather data a selfadministered five Likert scale questionnaire was employed. Data analysis was done using Excel 
and SPSS version 20.0 and data were displayed in tables. Frequencies, percentages, mean, and 
standard deviation were calculated using descriptive statistics. Pearman ’Rank correlation and 
ordinal regression were done for inferential statistics. The results from this study showed the 
predictors of teamwork studied which were abilities of the members of the team, team trust and 
team spirit or esprit de corps to have a strong relationship with employee performance. In 
addition, team trust and team spirit were found to positively affect the employee performance. 
Team trust showed a statistical significance while team spirit did not. Team members ‘abilities 
were found to negatively affect employee performance. However, this was not significant. 
Therefore, the study recommended ensuring a working environment that inspires team trust among 
teachers.

manuscripts.title: Humanism of Pandemics: An Essay in Public Health Policy and African  Philosophy
manuscripts.abstract:
We have argued in another paper that there is an African way of knowing which is purely and 
cognitively different from the Western episteme or paradigm of knowledge production. The 
question of the efficacy, potency scientificity and side effects of African traditional medicine should 
not be settled within the Western framework of ‘knowing’ but rather within the ontological and 
existential paradigm or context which birthed that medicine. It is purely illogical and anti-modus 
ponens to question the efficacy of African traditional medicine without proper regards and 
consultations of the methodologies in African science. Thus, using the hermeneutic method, this 
paper examines the efficacy of African traditional medicine, and it also mirrors the human face of 
pandemics such as the morality of isolation and the implication of social distancing. It concludes 
that one lesson from the corona pandemics, say, is the need for a synergy between methodologies 
in African medicine or sophistication of African traditional medicine. This work concludes that 
the methodologies of African traditional medicine show the efficacy and potency of the medicine 
in responding to pandemics such as Covid-19.

manuscripts.title: Contribution of Maternity Leave on Employee Commitment in Security and  Cleaning Companies in Rwanda
manuscripts.abstract:
This study investigated the contribution of maternity leave on employee commitment in Rwanda. This 
research employed descriptive research design. It describes the perspectives of respondents regarding 
maternity leave and women's performance in selected female casual and permanent employees of 
private institutions in Kigali. Regression also was used to determine the effect of maternity leave on 
women's Job performance. Data was collected using the questionnaire. In order to measure the 
relationship between Maternity leave and employee commitment, regression analysis was used, and 
the results indicated that the findings of the model summary one showed that employee commitment 
results showed the adjusted R2 of 0.629 representing 62.9% indicating that Maternity leave benefits 
contribute to Employee commitment while 0.371 representing 37.1% of employee commitment 
comes from other variables which not include in model 1. In the end selected companies are 
recommended to provide a special leave without pay to mothers at least 8 weeks for them to get time 
and be with their newborns fully. They are also recommended to provide one hour of breastfeeding 
in the morning and one hour in the evening to enhance the mother - childcare responsibilities. But 
also, effective policies should be put in place to promote employee job performance in selected 
companies, especially among female workers.

manuscripts.title: Maternal Death Audit: Exploratory Analysis of Maternal Death Dataset
manuscripts.abstract:
In 2015, Rwanda made significant strides in achieving the Millennium Development Goals 
(MDGs) 4 and 5, which relate to reducing child and maternal mortality. However, to maintain 
these achievements, evidence-based interventions must be implemented to reduce preventable 
deaths further. This study aims to utilize Rwanda's maternal death data from 2019 to 2022 to 
identify cases of maternal mortality and the factors associated with it. Additionally, the study aims 
to explore the relationship between variables associated with maternal mortality, specifically 
those linked to indirect causes. The investigation utilized a cross-sectional descriptive 
methodology to examine maternal mortality data in Rwanda. These datasets are from different 
sources but we mainly focus on the maternal death audit dataset. This comprehensive dataset 
encompasses maternal deaths in all districts, including those that occur within the community. The
analysis involved exploratory and assocition analyses as the primary methods. An analysis of the 
data set reveals that 80% of fatal cases are caused directly. The top causes of direct death are 
obstetric, hypertensive, and pregnancy-related complications, which together contribute to 76% 
of maternal deaths. The results also indicate that delays are a problem, which could be related to 
the patient, care provider, or transportation. Correlation analysis shows a significant association 
between the type of delay and the type of facility, with a coefficient of correlation. This association 
also exists between the type of facility and the mode of delivery. Additionally, there is an 
association between the mode of delivery and the level of healthcare providers. 
The study suggests that there is a need for capacity building to increase the knowledge and skills 
of healthcare providers. It also suggests that the healthcare system should find solutions to delays 
where possible, as this variable also contributes significantly to maternal deaths.

manuscripts.abstract:

commercial banks keep decreasing. Objective of the study is to assess the effect of risk management 
on non-performing loans in commercial banks in Rwanda. Researchers assume that there is no 
significant effect of risk management on reduction of non-performing loans in commercial banks 
in Rwanda. This research used descriptive survey research design. Population of the study are 
76 employees of Equity bank and Cogebank. These are composed of all manager, head of 
department, credit team, risk management team, audit team and financial department team of both 
Equity Bank Rwanda Plc headquarter and Cogebanque Rwanda Plc headquarter. The researcher 
used universal sampling technique and selected all the identified members of the population as the 
part of the study. Results for hypothesis testing indicated that the adjusted R2 is 0.880 indicating 
that the risk management components contribute to the reduction of non-performing loans by 
88.0%, while 0.120 representing 12.0% of reduction of non-performing loans comes from other 
variables that are not included in the model test. The selected commercial banks were 
recommended to find ways to improve their profitability levels since both of them were 
experiencing low levels of ROA of around 1 to 2%, yet the accepted good level of ROA is 5%
